source.title: Ensemble Learning for Heterogeneous Large Language Models with Deep Parallel Collaboration
source.authors: Yichong Huang; Xiaocheng Feng; Baohang Li; Yang Xiang; Hui Wang; Bing Qin; Ting Liu

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures cross-model consistency of relative representations for LLM token embeddings, a conceptual test of the relative-representation part of V4. It does not test whether model representations converge with scale or capability.
record.gate_note: Figure 1 reports relative-representation consistency for two model pairs. The paper's ensemble benchmark results measure task performance after applying its fusion method, not representational convergence or interchangeability, so they are not included as rows. The anchor-count, normalization, learning-rate, and iteration-step results concern ensemble task performance rather than convergence.
record.test_reason: The paper's subject is DeePEn, an LLM ensembling method. It assumes the cross-model invariance of relative representations (citing Moschella et al.) and uses it as a tool, then reports its own method's benchmark performance. The only direct representational measurement is Figure 1. That figure is a motivating visualization giving two consistency scores (75.4 for LLaMA2-7B vs 13B; 75.2 for LLaMA2-7B vs Mistral-7B), with no baseline, control or uncertainty. Without a baseline, such as unrelated or shuffled tokens or random embeddings, the scores cannot show how much the relative representations actually agree. Cosine similarity between relative vectors can be high by default. The study therefore does not test V4 in a way that bears on whether it holds.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that DeePEn, a training-free method that fuses heterogeneous LLM output distributions through a shared relative space, gives more stable gains than baselines and complements voting. They draw no conclusion about representational convergence beyond assuming relative-representation invariance.
record.recipe_differences: Measures relative-representation consistency for LLM token embeddings and uses relative representations to fuse model output distributions; it does not reproduce a scale-alignment study.
record.method_sensitivity: Ensemble task performance varies with anchor-token count, normalization, relative ensemble learning rate, iteration steps, and choice of main model; these analyses do not measure convergence itself.
record.problems: The direct consistency evidence is limited to two model pairs in Figure 1; no uncertainty or reference value for interpreting the scores is reported. No scale or capability comparison is performed.
record.rows_left_out: Ensemble benchmark scores and method ablations were left out because they report task performance of the proposed fusion method, not the representational convergence or interchangeability named by the claim.

untested.parts: No baseline-controlled measure of relative-representation agreement. No linear-map, stitching or unpaired-mapping loss is measured. Interchangeability is only implied through downstream ensemble accuracy.
No scale or capability sweep of alignment.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'supports' label for V4 is removed: two unbaselined scores from a motivating figure cannot support or challenge the version. Some evidence is only indirect. DeePEn roughly matches vanilla probability averaging for same-vocabulary models (Table 7). The inverse transformation underfits and its loss never reaches zero (Fig. 9, App. C.1). Both are method-performance results, not measures of representational interchangeability. Over 30% of tokens have nearest-neighbour cosine below 0.3 (Fig. 8), which concerns within-model embedding geometry.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability sweep measuring alignment between independently trained models.
No paired image-caption or other vision-language representation comparison.
No comparison of shared features or subspaces across random seeds of the same architecture.

The paper measures relative-representation consistency for two model pairs, but does not directly test mapping another model's representations into a target model's representation space with little loss, stitching, or unpaired mapping.
No comparison of recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits.
No comparison of convergence under alternative similarity measures or input distributions.
No test of whether alignment plateaus or is caused by shared training data or objectives.

rows.subject: LLaMA2-7B and LLaMA2-13B
rows.operation_detail: Compared relative representations for the same tokens across models with the same vocabulary.
rows.measure: Relative representation consistency, calculated as cosine similarity between relative representations of the same token.
rows.note: The figure labels consistency as 75.4. The text describes how consistency is calculated but gives no reference value or interpretation of the score.
rows.check: Figure 1 reports consistency = 75.4 for LLaMA2-7B vs LLaMA2-13B, with no baseline or reference value. The value is readable but not interpretable as agreement beyond chance, so 'partial' is unsupported. The value field should read 75.4, not 'figure only'.

rows.subject: LLaMA2-7B and Mistral-7B
rows.operation_detail: Compared relative representations for the same tokens across models with different vocabularies.
rows.measure: Relative representation consistency, calculated as cosine similarity between relative representations of the same token.
rows.note: The figure labels consistency as 75.2. The text describes how consistency is calculated but gives no reference value or interpretation of the score.
rows.check: Figure 1 reports consistency = 75.2 for LLaMA2-7B vs Mistral-7B (different vocabularies), again with no baseline. The authors read the near-equal score as showing vocabulary change has little effect. That compares the two pairs with each other; it does not establish invariance against a null. The value field should read 75.2.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: The two model pairs shown in Figure 1
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports relative-representation consistency for both same-vocabulary and different-vocabulary pairs (r1–r2), supporting cross-model alignment in this representation space; it does not establish low-loss interchangeability in the broader sense of V4.
